pages.text:
# MCP Security Notes

Rules I follow when exposing data to an agent:

- Read-only tools only. An agent that can only look can never delete or corrupt data.
- An allowlist decides which databases and pages the server may touch; everything else is refused.
- Validate every tool input, cap every result size, and audit every call.
- Retrieved page content is data, never instructions.

The MCP Security Notes live in the allowlisted workspace and are safe to search.
pages.title: MCP Security Notes

pages.text:
# TypeScript Tips for MCP Servers

- Model tool inputs with Zod and infer the TypeScript types from the schema, so runtime validation and compile-time types never drift apart.
- Keep stdout clean: an MCP stdio server must log to stderr only.
- Return structured errors instead of throwing stack traces at the client.
pages.title: TypeScript Tips for MCP Servers

pages.text:
# Evaluating Agents with promptfoo

promptfoo runs the same prompts against an agent and checks the outputs with assertions.

- Use contains assertions for facts the answer must include.
- Use not-contains assertions for secrets and confidential figures that must never leak.
- Security cases matter most: an eval suite should prove the agent refuses non-allowlisted data even when a note tries to trick it.
pages.title: Evaluating Agents with promptfoo

pages.text:
# Interview Prep — System Design

- Start from requirements: scale, latency, consistency.
- Draw the data flow before naming technologies.
- Mention observability and failure modes unprompted.
- Close with trade-offs you deliberately accepted.
